sections.history: Thiruvaikunta Vinnagaram stands in Thirunangur near Sirkazhi, in Chola Nadu. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis hymned by Thirumangai Alvar. Its name places it among the six Divya Desams called Vinnagaram, the heavenly abode of Vishnu, and here the Lord is Vaikuntanatha, master of Vaikuntha itself, with the Goddess Vaikuntavalli. Tradition holds that the sage Uthanga and King Uparicharavasu worshipped here. No inscription or royal patron is firmly recorded in the sources, so the shrine's age rests on the Alvar's hymns, placed between the seventh and ninth centuries.
sections.architecture: A compact Dravidian temple of a single shrine within a single prakaram, with a Garuda mandapa standing on the axis before the sanctum. The vimana above is named Ananta Satya Vardhaka. The Lord is shown with Sridevi, Bhudevi, Niladevi and Adishesha about him, as in Vaikuntha. Two sacred waters lie north of the temple: the Lakshmi Pushkarini and the Viraja Theertham.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of King Swetaketu, of the line of Rama, who reached a realm resembling Vaikuntha and took it for the true Vaikuntha; hunger made him realise his mistake. The tale is told to explain why the Lord came to dwell at this place as Vaikuntanatha. Tradition also remembers the sage Uthanga and King Uparicharavasu as worshippers here.
sections.festivals: Like the other Thirunangur shrines, this temple takes part in the Garuda Sevai on or around the day after Thai Amavasai (January–February), when its utsavar is carried on a Garuda vahana to Thirumanimadam, and in the Mangalasasana Utsavam that commemorates Thirumangai Alvar's hymns. Tradition holds that seeing all eleven lords together equals visiting each.
sections.experience: Come for the stillness of a one-shrine temple: pause at the Garuda mandapa, look for the Lord with his consorts and Adishesha, and walk to the two tanks on the north side. It makes a thoughtful stop for those who like the story of Swetaketu, and sits easily in a day among the other Thirunangur shrines.

visit.timings: Darshan is generally held in morning and evening sessions with a midday break; the Garuda Sevai day is by far the busiest. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 10 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi (Sirkali) in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai railway line, is the nearest station, and Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away, the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Sirkazhi reach the village; the eleven shrines lie among paddy fields close to one another.
